stem: Why is cation-exchange capacity relevant when evaluating a root-zone medium?
choices: It describes the rate at which roots exchange oxygen and carbon dioxide with the medium, making it a direct measure of root-zone aeration capacity
It describes a medium's ability to retain and exchange positively charged ions, which can influence nutrient buffering and availability
It describes the total dissolved-salt concentration of irrigation water and is therefore another expression of electrical conductivity in the root zone
It measures how strongly a medium resists changes in pH, so a higher value indicates that root-zone pH will remain stable under normal feeding
rationale: Cation-exchange capacity describes the capacity of a medium to hold and exchange cations. It can influence how nutrients are retained and buffered in the root zone.
